::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 24. 1865  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS. 55384 (1): P. 397
:::

My dear Miss Yonge	
[I](people/person_939.qmd)ought to have acknowledged the [copy](cmy_books/cmybook_62.qmd) for the new [number](organizations/other_78.qmd)earlier, but I wanted to write you a longer letter which I cant do today after all.

I would be glad to see what more you have written of [Bethlehem](organizations/other_177.qmd), when you have satisfied yourself - or at least approximately - who could satisfy themselves on such a subject. The young [Artist](people/person_500.qmd) is ready to [work](organizations/other_167.qmd) whenever you like.

Shall I [pay](organizations/other_160.qmd) the monthly sums to your [banker](organizations/other_169.qmd) in London, or send you a cheque? I have also the £200 for the [Clever Woman](cmy_books/cmybook_58.qmd) to pay.

It is indeed glorious weather. You should see us now at Tooting.

Yours most truly
A. Macmillan
